title: The AWARE framework — leading teams through gen AI
blurb: Why great innovations fail to scale: workers resist gen AI when it threatens competence, autonomy and relatedness. AWARE is the leadership playbook to win them back.
body:
From the HBR cover story "Why Great Innovations Fail to Scale" (Hermann, Puntoni & Morewedge). The core thesis: gen AI succeeds or stalls depending on whether it satisfies or frustrates three psychological needs — competence (feeling effective), autonomy (feeling in control), and relatedness (meaningful connection).

When those needs are threatened, you get resistance, disengagement and even sabotage: one 2025 survey found 85% of leaders use gen AI regularly but only 51% of workers do.

The AWARE framework

  • Acknowledge how gen AI affects workers' competence, autonomy and relatedness — open dialogue, surface concerns, don't suppress them.
  • Watch for maladaptive coping (task avoidance, withdrawal, "shadow" AI use) so you can intervene before performance declines.
  • Align training, mentoring, job design and feedback with workers' psychological needs.
  • Redesign roles around human–AI complementarity — give AI the repetitive/data-heavy work, give people empathy, creativity, judgment.
  • Empower workers to shape how AI affects their work — transparency, inclusion, participation in the rollout.

The payoff: supporting core psychological needs turns gen AI from a perceived threat into a trusted copilot. (Full reconstruction available as a Word document.)
